en.sup: Supplied in English. The Hebrew verb has no object; the tithe of the verses before is understood.

01.r: The worshipper who lives far off trades the tithed produce for silver.
01.n: The verb is the ordinary word for 'give'; the brief's lexicon lists 'sell' and 'exchange' among its senses. A perfect with 'and', carrying on from the 'if' of the verse before: 'then you shall'. YLT renders the form literally, 'thou hast given it'.
t: Thou shalt sell them all, and turn them

02.n: Our register renders this word 'silver'. Gesenius: silver, so called from its pale colour; the brief's lexicon gives silver, money. The translations all say 'money'.

03.r: The silver is tied up safely for the journey.
03.n: Gesenius gives 'to bind together, into a bundle or roll' and cites this verse. The Geneva and BSB say 'take', the DRC 'carry'.

04.r: The silver received for the tithe.
04.n: The same word as before, now with 'the': the silver just received.

06.r: The worshipper still makes the journey, with silver in place of produce.
06.n: A perfect with 'and', continuing the instruction. YLT keeps the perfect form, 'and gone'.

08.r: The one sanctuary the LORD will choose.

09.r: Introduces the description of the place.
09.n: Hebrew says 'which ... will choose in it'; English needs only 'that'.

10.r: The LORD, not the worshipper, picks the place.

11.r: The personal name of Israel's God.

12.n: The form is plural but the meaning is singular. The DRC leaves it out.

13.r: Points back to the place: 'which he chooses, in it'.
13.n: 'In it', a pronoun that repeats the place after the verb. English does not need it, so it is counted with 'that'; YLT's 'on which' reflects it.

_extra.2: αὐτὰ (them): the Greek supplies the object, the tithes, which the Hebrew leaves unstated.

01.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives none. ἀποδίδωμι is the verb our register renders 'give back'; of goods, as here, it means to sell.

02.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives none. ἀργύριον is the word our register renders 'silver'.

03.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives none. λήμψῃ, 'you shall take', where the Hebrew says 'bind up'; the Geneva's and BSB's 'take' agree with this Greek.

04.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives none.

05.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives none. The Greek says 'in your hands', plural.

06.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives none.

07.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives none.

13.n: αὐτόν, 'it', the place: the Greek keeps the Hebrew's pronoun as the object of 'choose'.
